resolved_prompt: Compose one continuous single-view vertical image built around exactly one clearly adult woman as the only figure. Every visible face, body, and hand belongs to this same woman. Place a clearly visible strip of background above her entire hairstyle, and keep her complete crown, face, and both eyes clearly readable. The second lighting direction has authority over every actual source shape, direction, and illumination color. Keep the face and requested visible eyes readable, and make each source named by that direction visibly distinct. Give its named reflected light or fill a separate readable role. Carry the first style only through set shape, material color, surface, atmosphere, and edge treatment. Use a photorealistic adult editorial material treatment with broad curved set paths, flowing graphic shadows, and repeated organic shapes; garnet, sapphire, emerald, and restrained metallic-gold material fields; fine paper fibers across backdrop and graphic shadow shapes; upward set panels, rising decorative forms, and restrained metallic glints; and hard separated silhouette and graphic edges with few controlled breaks. Treat these as material, set, pigment, and graphic properties; the second lighting direction alone supplies every actual source and illumination color. The image uses enveloping diffuse light with open shadows and gentle local contrast and late golden light with neutral readable shadows and restrained saturation. Resolve both directions on the same adult subject. Give every named visual cue an obvious, concrete location on the face, clothing, silhouette, lighting, or environment. Preserve the selected medium and keep the face, eyes, visible hands, joints, garment construction, and spatial relationships coherent. Finish the single scene cleanly with text-free, logo-free, watermark-free imagery. The second lighting direction is the final illumination blueprint: all visible illumination comes only from its named sources, colors, and geometry. Its named reflected light or fill remains visibly separate from the key. The first style contributes shape, material palette, surface, atmosphere, and edge treatment.
